title: Dam Haji Seorang
mood: wry, lonesome, warming to a smile
subject: Since his dam haji opponent moved to Johor Bahru, 71-year-old Mat Zin has played both sides with bottle caps against an empty stool under a mango tree in Lenggong, until the young Bangladeshi pump attendant from across the road sits down and beats him.
caption: Malay 12-bar blues shuffle in the slow-triplet Blues Gang tradition. A harmonica answering each vocal line with short fills, a bottleneck slide electric guitar with light overdrive and lazy slides, a walking electric bass, brushed drums in a slow triplet shuffle, and soft Hammond organ swells under the chorus. Dry warm live-room mix, harmonica and voice close. Male weathered warm baritone singing every line with a steady melody. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 84 BPM, E major. Wry, lonesome, warming to a smile. No rap, no autotune, no trap drums, no synth pads, no dangdut, no heavy-metal distortion.
lyrics:
[Intro - harmonica, slide guitar, brushed shuffle]
[Verse 1]
Bawah pokok mangga di Lenggong
Mat Zin susun tutup botol
Sebelah dia bangku kosong
Haji Daud dah pindah ke JB
[Pre-Chorus]
Dia gerak buah merah, dia gerak buah putih
Menang pun dia, kalah pun dia
[Chorus]
Main dam dua belah, dua-dua aku
Bangku kosong tak pernah marah
Tak pernah ketawa, tak pernah bantah
Petang panjang, mangga jatuh
[Verse 2]
Budak pam minyak kat seberang jalan
Datang berdiri, tengok papan
Rafiq nama dia, orang Dhaka
Dia duduk atas bangku kosong
[Pre-Chorus]
Satu langkah dia, aku termenung
Tiga buah aku kena lompat
[Chorus]
Main dam dua orang, aku kalah
Kalah pun aku, aku senyum
Bangku itu dah ada orang
Ketawa dia macam Haji Daud
[Bridge - harmonica solo]
Esok petang datang lagi, Rafiq?
[Chorus]
Main dam dua orang, aku kalah
Kalah pun aku, tak mengapa
Bangku itu dah ada orang
Bawah mangga, petang panjang
[Outro - slide guitar, organ fading]
Tutup botol merah, tutup botol putih
